title: I Let the Welding-Booth Hood Log Catch the Intern Who Skipped It

parts.text: I signed booth 4 at 10:17 a.m. and intern Zed struck an arc with an unsigned hood. The sheet said: HOOD ON THE LOG. CURTAIN CLOSED. NO UNSIGNED ARCS. I was twenty-eight, student, holding a hood card. Zed shrugged. "Interns are the spark." I photographed the sheet, the card, and the open curtain. Then I asked for the hood log. At 10:23 the shop safety pinged why Zed's name was on an unsigned arc. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Shop safety can see Zed's unsigned hood on booth 4 during an open-curtain arc.

social.video_title: The intern struck an arc with an unsigned hood — Part 1/2
social.description: Welding booth, a hood log, an open curtain. I logged the skip. Would you have asked safety?

parts.text: Zed called it a tack until safety asked for the still. I printed the log, the sheet, and the card. The hood signed. Zed closed curtains and told the next intern tacks were always about optics. Optics is a word interns use when logs exist. Booth policy now has a second line: INTERNS SIGN THE HOOD. I keep booth 4. Zed brown-bags the jokes. The bay finally looks like a sheet, not a spark. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Hood log, closed curtain, and a second line. Was a tack ever unsigned?
